, with resale opportunities, the auctioneer should not worry about the information rents of high-value bidders, but rather focus on the low-value bidder, who may be induced to bid below her valuation if she expects to win the auction.

, when resale is possible, the optimal mechanism is a Vickrey auction, with bidder-specific reserve price, that is, a second-price auction in which a bidder is not allowed to bid less than the highest bid he has ever placed in any auction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the revenue-maximizing mechanism can be very sensitive to the assumptions about resale opportunities, and that the optimal mechanism can be very different from the standard auction.
the standard auction is not robust to the possibility of resale, and that the optimal auction depends on the nature of the resale opportunities.
